01 / The whole system

How Stock
Backtest works.

The program uses saved company data and prices to select stocks. It then checks how those stocks performed.

This guide explains each part, how the parts connect, and why some runs take longer. You do not need to read the code.

Saved dataOne set of selection rulesFour ways to use itNo downloads during a backtest

The main data flow

Save once. Prepare once.
Select many times.

A cache is saved data that the program can use again. Select a step to see its job.

1. The source data stays on your computer.

The raw folder holds the saved inputs. Ordinary preparation and backtests read these files. They do not contact the data supplier.

The browser and Python use the same selection rules. They use different prepared records for different dates.

02 / Three ways to use it

The date choice sets the path.

Latest picks work in the saved HTML page. Custom dates and random dates need the local Python service. A January study is a custom schedule every 12 months from 1 January; there is no January mode.

Choose when the test runs.

In latest mode, select Screen latest. Clear Auto-run when settings change to edit several settings before a screen. The browser remembers this choice. In Historical backtest mode, select Add to queue. Every dated test runs from the queue on the server. This mode has no immediate run and no Auto-run.

An amber notice appears when the displayed latest picks differ from the current settings. It clears after a matching screen or when you restore the settings. A dated result is a stored record, and the builder shows no notice for it.

A latest screen of a chain that the page cannot screen offline runs on the local service. The button shows Screening… until the answer arrives. The server keeps these screens in memory for 24 hours, up to four recent runs. The page keeps no record of a screen. After a reload, select Screen latest again.

Keep the server computer awake and its terminal open. One calculation runs at a time. Stopping the server cancels active work and waits for cleanup. The queue then runs an interrupted test again.

These controls are in the current source. Installing a committed revision and reloading the page makes them available in the native website. Source edits do not change an already running server.

How do I queue tests for an overnight run?

Select Historical backtest, set a fixed or random-date test, then select Add to queue. This is the only way to run a dated test. You can type a test name in the box beside Add to queue. An empty name describes the final Rank, then the other steps in step order. It adds the rebalance interval when that is not 12 months, and the market when that is not US. An example is Ranks 1–10 · EBITDA / EV yield · highest first · quarterly · Market cap ≥ $100M. Use Open Runs & saved to see the test. Change the settings to add another test.

Tests run one at a time. You can close this page or lock your phone. Keep the server computer awake and its terminal open. A failed test remains visible and does not stop the next test.

Runs & saved shows the queue below In progress. Select All, US, Hong Kong or Tokyo above the groups to show the tests of one market in the two groups. Each button shows its count. The page remembers the last choice. The running test is first. The waiting tests follow in queue order. Failed tests, stopped tests and completed tests that are not moved are last. A running row shows its progress with its status. Select Details at the end of a row to read its settings and to find its actions.

Select Edit settings to hold a waiting test. Use the strategy controls to change its parameters. Save to return it to the queue, or cancel to keep its previous settings. The name box shows the name of the held test. If that name is the automatic name for the old settings, Save gives the test the automatic name for the new settings. A name that you typed stays. Moving this test or its neighbor does not invalidate the edit. Each edit has an identity and a settings version. The server keeps its latest Save or Cancel receipt. An exact retry stays safe after the test starts. If a response is lost, the page checks the receipt or offers a retry. If another browser ends or replaces the hold, the form becomes available and keeps its current settings. Held edits stay held after a page or server restart. Use Release hold to return an abandoned edit to the queue. Running settings cannot change. While an edit owns the form, copying another test cannot replace its draft. Save or cancel the edit first. The same form check protects all settings restoration paths.

Move up and Move down change waiting order. Tune copies the settings to Build strategy for a new test. It makes the name box empty. Pause queue lets the active test finish and prevents the next test from starting. Stop test cancels the selected active test. The next test waits for worker and cache cleanup.

A completed test moves to Saved backtests automatically. Saved backtests shows the saved library. Before the move, Open result in Details restores stored charts, all trial stocks and downloads. No calculation runs. A full library shows Completed — waiting for saved slot. Other save failures keep the complete result in the queue and show a retry notice. The server retries without recalculation, including while execution is paused or the engine is unavailable. The library checks prior transfer receipts and free slots before copying a result. It checks both again when it saves. Failed and stopped tests remain in In progress. Deletion confirms one selected record. Stop a running test before deleting it. During a transfer, refresh and retry deletion after it finishes.

The queue holds up to 100 records that are still visible. Successful transfers free queue slots. It uses data/backtest-queue.sqlite. Keep this durable file during preparation, cleanup and deployment. The queue is separate from the 100-slot saved library. The saved copy commits before duplicate queue result bytes are removed. There is no automatic eviction.

One consumer lock protects queue execution across server instances. Queue transactions end before financial ownership starts. A latest screen on the service or a data rebuild can delay queue work. It does not turn waiting tests into lock-timeout failures. Shutdown waits for normal engine cleanup and returns unfinished work to the queue. A successor recovers running records only after it owns the consumer lock. Stop intent remains cancelled.

A random seed is stored at admission. The full trial date plan is stored before calculation and reused after interruption. Changing waiting calculation parameters discards the old plan. Renaming a test keeps its dates. Tests use saved financial inputs available when they execute. Completed artifacts keep their original priced results.

How do I keep a completed backtest?

A completed queue test is saved automatically. The page has no other save. The record keeps the settings used for that result, all traded stocks and all returns.

Open Runs & saved to find a record. The saved records are the rows below Saved backtests. Select the name of a row to inspect its recorded settings, charts, stock tables and CSV downloads in Result review. Your unfinished strategy draft stays unchanged. No calculation runs. Later data changes do not rewrite saved results. Saved metric labels, filter labels and warnings also stay with the original result. Earlier saved records still open without changing their stored data.

A saved January result opens in the dated view. Its book years become dated periods when it is read. Period dates that were not stored show the book year. The stored record is not rewritten.

Select Details at the end of a saved row, then Tune, to load its parameters into the current strategy controls. Adjust the controls, then select Add to queue. Tune starts no calculation. The displayed result keeps its original values. The editable controls keep the copied test’s labels. A saved choice that is no longer supported stays visible as unavailable. Custom formulas retain their captured revisions and labels. Random dates restore the recorded seed for repeatable tuning. A held queue edit can stay open while you inspect another result. Save or cancel the edit before copying settings into its draft.

A random-date record includes every trial’s trade dates, traded stocks and period returns. It also keeps the seed and distribution summary. Trial inspection reads these saved stocks. It does not recalculate a book.

The library has 100 slots. Each finished test uses one. When all slots are used, delete a chosen record, and the next finished test moves in. The program never removes an older record to make room. Deletion asks for confirmation. The displayed result stays available after its saved record is deleted.

Each record has a stable UUID database ID. Open Details of its row to read the ID. Select Rename there, enter a name, then select Save name or Cancel. Renaming changes only the name. It keeps the ID, creation date, settings and all result bytes. Automatic queue updates wait until you finish renaming, so they do not interrupt typing.

The list starts with the newest saved record. Select the Name, CAGR or Saved heading to sort the Saved backtests rows. Select it again to reverse the order. The CAGR column shows CAGR for January and fixed dates. It shows mean trial CAGR for random dates. Different windows and test types can differ. A missing CAGR stays last in the two directions. Equal values use the saved date and ID for a stable order.

A successful rename or deletion stays confirmed if a later list refresh fails. The page keeps the confirmed change in its list. Select Refresh in Runs & saved to check records from other browser sessions.

Open Details of a saved row to read its recorded settings. This does not open its result or change the strategy form. Details shows the settings in plain wording, for example Market cap ≥ $100M. The headline, the saved ID and the actions follow. A closed Exact recorded values list shows every recorded row with its exact text. The page reads the stored result one time, when Details opens.

Tick saved rows, then select Compare to compare them. The box in the heading ticks every row shown. Select Lock ticked to lock the ticked records. A locked row shows Locked, and you cannot delete it. Select Unlock ticked to remove the lock. Select Delete ticked to delete the ticked records that are not locked, after one confirmation. The heading, the bar and the column headings stay at the top of the window when you scroll the rows. A panel above the Saved backtests rows shows one column for each ticked test, in list order. The first rows are the requested settings that differ, or the words Same settings. The headline rows follow them. A closed disclosure contains every setting and, for a random-date test, six more measures. In that list, an amber row with the word Different identifies a setting that differs. If two tests differ in a setting that has the same plain wording, that row shows the exact text. A measure that a test does not have shows a dash. Clear removes every tick. A change of market also removes every tick. A failed read shows its cause above the rows.

Comparison reads stored results without recalculation. Legacy and current calendars compare in one form. Documented omission defaults keep their meaning. Reordering AND conditions or repeating an identical condition changes no result. Strict operators, unknown settings and stored labels remain visible. A difference uses the exact recorded value. Performance shows 2 decimals. A value below 0.01 shows 2 significant digits. Requested engine and recorded producer are separate. An older result without producer evidence stays unidentified. Random tests show requested seed policy, the recorded seed and stored trial statistics. Mean trial CAGR is not one portfolio return. Percentiles are not confidence intervals. One-line notices identify different test types, requested windows and recorded observation windows.

Queue transfers save one independent record per completed test. A durable import receipt prevents duplicates after interruption. The receipt survives saved-record deletion. Recovery keeps later renames and explicit deletion. Archived queue receipts cannot restart or redisplay old tests. Existing open result readers keep their original bytes when duplicate queue storage is released.

Records live on the server computer in data/saved-backtests.sqlite. Browser sessions using that runtime share the library. The records survive browser restarts, server restarts and prepared-cache rebuilds. Keep this file when you clean caches. Back it up with your user data. A saved HTML page needs the local service to use the library.

Prepared in advance · Runs in the browser

A screen for the latest saved session.

Prepared latest records→Data inside the HTML→Browser selection→Stock list

Latest means the latest completed session of the selected market in the saved data. It does not mean a live market feed.

A company needs a price on that exact session. The saved company list must mark it as listed. Old stopped prices are excluded. These picks have no future holding return.

Prepared when needed · Uses the local Python service

A test on your chosen calendar.

Browser request→Local Python service→Saved or new dated books→Results in the browser

Choose One fixed schedule, then the start date, end date and rebalance interval. Tick Custom week/month interval to show its count and unit. Random trials and Advanced show only when you select random dates. Opening this view runs nothing by itself. Original runs this test. It supports the 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24-month presets and custom 1–104 weeks or 1–24 months.

Trade dates move forward to a saved session of the selected market. The end mark moves back to a session. A new entry session can need an entry sheet. Another exit reuses that sheet. The run closes only the selected stocks.

A request for the removed January mode fails with UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY at /mode. It is never converted to a dated schedule.

Many dated tests · Uses the local Python service

The same strategy on different trade dates.

Sample trade dates→Calculate with Original→Calculate complete trials→Save and recover completed trials→Compare trial results

For each trial, the program selects one trading session from each frequency block. The last partial block also participates. Actual holding periods can have different lengths.

Trials use the same start and end window. Strategy and SPY hold cash until the first trade. Original plans shared missing entry sheets and calculates them ahead. One parent saves completed trials and presents them in recorded order.

New runs use fresh dates by default. A seed is a number that lets you repeat the date choices. Use the same settings and seed to repeat a batch.

What happens when you double-click start.cmd?

Run backtest-web.cmd in Windows Terminal, or double-click start.cmd. The website stays attached to this terminal on 0.0.0.0:3000. Open http://127.0.0.1:3000 on this computer. The terminal shows server logs. Press Ctrl+C to stop. A new launch stops this project’s identified server and starts current code in the new terminal. This also replaces an older background instance. A startup lock serializes preparation and binding. A lifetime lock stays held until the listener and all request threads close. A stopped HTTP endpoint does not release ownership. A replacement waits up to 30 seconds, then asks you to wait or stop the old terminal and retry. Python prepares stale caches and builds before it opens the browser. An ordinary launch starts with the installed revision. The terminal checks committed main once a day at 07:00 Hong Kong time. Maintenance stops the server, installs any new commit, refreshes FMP data, prepares saved inputs and rebuilds the website before accepting work. It runs with no new commit too. A missed schedule waits until the next day. Many commits in one day cause one scheduled maintenance cycle. Existing terminals keep their loaded behavior until restarted. Add --latest to install the newest main commit at launch. Uncommitted saves do not trigger updates. An unrelated port owner is left running; the website uses a free port.

Development and runtime

Edit in WSL.
Run native Windows code.

The WSL source checkout owns code and Git history. The Windows runtime owns saved market data, prepared databases, logs and local builds.

WSL source→Committed source deployment→Windows runtime

From WSL, run python3 tools/deploy.py --start. From Windows Terminal, run the installed backtest-web.cmd. The WSL launcher starts the installed revision with native Windows Python in that terminal. It checks main once a day at 07:00 Hong Kong time. Maintenance refreshes FMP inputs even with no new commit. It prepares the databases and website before accepting requests or queued work. A missed schedule waits until the next day. Run backtest-web.cmd --latest to install the newest main commit at launch. A fresh runtime installs main. Uncommitted edits and linked worktrees are excluded. The source checkout is a WSL clone of this repository. The runtime is a separate folder on the Windows filesystem, exported from a committed revision.

The source launcher locates tools/deploy.py relative to its command file. It can run from the WSL network path without changing CMD’s working directory. This fix stays in source until a committed revision containing it is installed.

What does deployment change?

Deployment publishes one exact Git commit. Normal server startup serves the installed revision and follows committed main at 07:00 Hong Kong time daily. Standalone publication and --check retain the installed commit from data/deployment.json. A fresh standalone publication requires an explicit revision; automatic startup selects main only with --latest, at the daily check or on a fresh runtime. Use python3 tools/deploy.py --revision <commit> --start from WSL to select a fixed revision without automatic updates. An explicit --revision HEAD fixes that launch to the resolved commit. Working-tree edits stay in WSL. The runtime has no separate Git repository. Source file hashes and the deployed commit are recorded in data/deployment.json. Only source files owned by the preceding deployment can be removed. Unexpected source edits or conflicting local files stop publication.

Raw data, databases, environments, logs, the local website build and baseline revision history stay on Windows. The runtime copy of the January report also stays there. Deployment never installs, replaces or removes that file, and nothing reads it. The tracked report is a frozen record. No command collects a runtime report into source.

How are running servers protected?

The entry point website/serve.py takes shared source ownership before importing website/server/app.py. It holds ownership through server cleanup. website/runtime_access.py owns this boundary. Deployment stops authenticated instances from this runtime, including alternate ports. It waits for process exit, then takes exclusive source ownership and financial cache ownership. Unknown listeners remain running.

An interrupted source publication leaves data/deployment.pending.json. Startup refuses to import the application while that journal exists. Run deployment again to finish the verified publication. Default retry selects the journal’s commit. It does not restore the older manifest commit after recovery. An explicit different revision is rejected before staging. Finish recovery before selecting another revision. Do not remove the journal to bypass recovery.

Automatic updates watch committed main in the registered WSL source. They do not fetch Git history. A source archive is ready before the old child receives its private stop marker. The server performs normal Ctrl+C cleanup, including during startup preparation. Deployment waits for the child to exit, then keeps the existing source and financial lock order. A latest screen in progress stops. Interrupted queued tests return to waiting with their recorded dates. Saved results and raw data stay in place. A missing Git observation keeps the installed revision; scheduled data refresh still runs. Failed updates retry automatically and preserve pending recovery. Ctrl+C stops this watcher and its own server. A server replaced by another terminal ends its old watcher. Refresh an open browser page after the new server is ready. Automatic restarts do not open another tab.

What does the development log record?

Each server process writes its own log in data/logs/website-<namespace>-<pid>.log. The data panel shows its path. Each line is one JSON event with a UTC time. The log never contains exception text, source lines, local variables, keys, provider URLs or response bodies. A failure keeps its error types, OS codes and stack locations. The logs stay local and are excluded from Git. Server and update-watcher lines in the terminal start with the local date and time. The three lines of a website build do not.

A long operation writes one event when it ends. The event gives the outcome, the wall seconds, the CPU seconds of the operation’s thread, stage seconds and counts. backtest.run covers each manual or queued calculation. It records the mode, the admission, the pool, the number of periods and trials, and the book statistics of random trials. Its stages include the admission wait, planning, book calculation, book writes, selection and result sealing. When worker processes evaluate the trials, the trials stage records their time and the event has no selection stage. Its CPU seconds do not include the workers. queue.test adds the result store time and the reason for a requeue. prepare.research records each preparation phase, the number of cached companies and the number of price series left out for a price spike. Compatible research builds reconcile changed typed rows. Cold, schema or fact-code builds replace the database. A cold build on worker processes records their time as the ranges stage. Its CPU seconds do not include the workers. prepare.daily records the previous and retained sheet headers. Research records per-company and shared fact changes. Daily preparation repairs only the affected sheet rows. startup.prepare and data.job cover startup and data-panel work. A request that takes one second or more writes http.slow with its route. The route has no identifiers and no query text.

Stages are measured regions. They can overlap, so they need not add up to the total seconds.

An operation that takes longer than one minute also reports progress. After its first minute, it writes a running line, and then one more every five minutes. The line gives the time so far, the last finished step and the time since it, the stage in progress when one is open, live counts and the process CPU time. During a data update, the line also gives the update stage and its completed and total counts, for example "work": {"stage": "sheets", "completed": 3250, "total": 15400}. The update records the sheets stage as a step when it ends. A report also counts for the operations around the reporter, which it names, for example startup and the daily cache around the research database. An operation with an open inner operation waits one more minute, so a long inner operation reports for it. An operation made of short inner operations then reports for itself. When a reporting operation ends, the operation around it reports at once, so the latest progress line stays current. A step of one minute or more writes a step line when it ends. A step that only waited for an inner operation writes no step line, because that operation’s end line already shows its time. An operation that ends within a minute writes only its end line. If a process stops during an operation, its last progress line shows where it was.

Run python3 -m tools.ops.log_summary from the project folder. It first lists unfinished operations with their latest progress line. Then it prints the median, 90th-percentile and longest time of each operation, its largest stage shares, the latest backtest runs, slow requests and failures. Add --days 7 to read only the last week. Reading never changes a log.

A log rotates at 5 MiB and keeps two older files. Startup removes logs that have had no write for 14 days. Then it removes the oldest logs of stopped servers in this process namespace until those logs total at most 50 files and 100 MiB. The file name holds the namespace: machine identity on Windows, boot and PID namespace on Linux, so a Linux reboot starts a new namespace. A log from another namespace or an older name format has no process to check. Only its age removes it, and it does not count toward these targets. When the namespace is unknown, only age applies. The log of a running server in this namespace stays, and so does a file that cannot be deleted. Cleanup errors never stop startup.

Where do tests run?

WSL runs source and synthetic checks. python3 tools/deploy.py --check deploys committed code and runs the installed Windows checks, including saved-data path checks, preparation and browser parity. It does not download market data. Each operating system has its own environment and compiled caches.

Markets and currency

One market per run. USD results.

Choose US, Hong Kong or Japan · Tokyo in the strategy or data panel. Hong Kong covers Main Board and GEM common stocks. Japan covers Tokyo listings. New forms use the broad cached-price pool. Restored US work retains its recorded pool. Available date bounds come from that market’s saved sessions.

All monetary thresholds, prices, returns and CAGR use USD. Foreign returns include unhedged exchange-rate changes. Cash earns 0% USD. SPY is always the S&P 500 total-return proxy. Asian dates use the previous completed US close. Date-only FX uses the previous completed daily fixing. Yield references remain US Treasury yields.

Foreign annual monetary values use the context date’s FX for every report year. Shares stay shares. Annual-share fiscal valuation is an approximation. Missing required FX or prices stay unavailable. FMP coverage, zero-heavy fields, later statement revisions, historical listing gaps and dividend adjustments limit the result. No per-company certification or automatic historical repair is required.

US raw paths stay unchanged. backtest/inputs/market.py names market policy and paths. Foreign inventory and index calendars live in raw/markets/<market>/. Suffixed annual files remain in raw/financial-inputs/ and adjusted prices in raw/px/. Native closes use raw/px-full/; direct FX uses raw/fx/USD<currency>.json. The existing transport, receipts and publishing owner save them. Scheduled refresh uses the existing cycle for markets already saved.

Prepared facts add company_markets, annual_metadata, foreign_reports, stock_native, local_sessions and fx_days. Book headers and lookup include market. The rendering owner embeds market-bound screens, filter choices and dates. Top-level options.market survives jobs, held edits, queue records, saved opening, comparisons and exports. Its omission on old records means US. Saved opening runs no calculation.

Catalog financial-parameters/4 uses market-annual/1 with the existing definition syntax version 3 and evaluator. A Hong Kong or Japan run uses the market-aware form of every formula in the strategy. You do not need to do anything. The draft sends the market when it captures the strategy. The capture then gives each formula, and each formula that it references, catalog /4 and market-annual/1. Named measures use their /4 revisions. A US run keeps each formula as saved. Saved variables and the draft do not change. Catalogs /1–/3 keep their recorded US meanings. Source fixtures establish no installed readiness, native Windows verification or real-cache coverage.

03 / One holding period

From a report to a portfolio.

A book describes one buy date and one sell or mark date. The dated engine prepares the requested stock group before it applies your final filters.

  1. Choose a usable annual report.

    US reports become available 90 days after year-end. HK and JP use reliable publication dates where available, otherwise four and three calendar months. Availability must be before the buy date. A report older than 800 days is excluded.

  2. Prepare the requested stock group.

    New forms use the broader group of companies with saved prices. Restored US work keeps its recorded original 250-name screen. Only the requested group is prepared. Neither group covers the full market.

  3. Estimate values at the buy date.

    US valuations use saved prices to update report market cap. Foreign valuations use annual basic weighted-average shares and a native unadjusted fiscal close, then rescale with adjusted prices. It adds report net debt to estimate enterprise value. A missing buy price excludes a stock.

    Some saved price series mix two price scales. One close is then at least 8 times, or at most 1/8 of, the closes on both sides. Preparation keeps no price of such a stock, so it has no buy price. Preparation prints the symbols that it left out.

  4. Prepare entry values, then close selected holdings.

    The program saves both supported EBITDA metrics for the requested entry and group. After ranking, it uses dividend-adjusted exit prices for selected holdings only.

  5. Run the ordered steps.

    The program reads your chosen group. It then runs your Filter and Rank steps in order. A Filter keeps the stocks that pass. A Rank orders the stocks that reach it and keeps its rank range. The last Rank sets the final ranks. Filters after it keep original ranks and add no replacements. The default chain filters size, then ranks by EBITDA/EV yield, highest first: lower multiples rank first.

  6. Calculate the portfolio result.

    Each selected stock starts with the same weight. The program averages their holding returns. It joins the USD periods and compares the result with SPY.

Period return = sum of selected stock returns ÷ actual selected stock count
What if a stock stops trading?

The historical engine uses its last available price. The proceeds stay as cash until the next rebalance. A listed bankruptcy override gives a total loss. Each override names a stock and the day of the loss. Only a book whose window contains that day takes the loss: after the entry day, through the exit day. The override list is currently empty.

Each holding shows how it exited. A normal exit shows Scheduled exit. The last period of a test shows Marked to date when it ends on the test's end date and not on a scheduled rebalance. Random and explicit trades always end that way. Last available price and Bankruptcy keep their labels. A saved book is shared by every schedule with the same dates, so the test applies the final label, not the book. Saved results keep the labels that they were saved with.

A later delisting does not change an earlier sale price. The original review covered 37 early stops. Additional stops in expanded or dated tests have not all received that review.

How are complete dated results calculated?

Fixed and explicit-date tests use one portfolio reducer in backtest/portfolio_results.py. It keeps all selected stock rows in rank order. Equal weights use the actual stock count. Signed contributions, period compounding, stopped proceeds and cash before the first trade keep their existing meaning. A complete empty period holds cash at 0% until rebalance. SPY keeps its period return. CAGR includes the full elapsed window.

Each period of a new dated result also has a daily curve: for each market session in the period, the mean return to date of the selected stocks and of SPY. A day without a close keeps the last price, as a stopped stock does. The last row holds the saved returns of the period, and the run fails if a stock's last value differs from its saved return. Thus no existing value changes. backtest/engines/original/curves.py reads the daily closes; an edit to it rebuilds no prepared data. The daily curve contract gives every rule.

The website obtains stored books through daily SQLite preparation. New dated captures select through the scalar executor over prepared sheet values. Existing legacy queue rows keep the SQL selector. The reducer can also emit one complete period at a time. A separate versioned evidence codec writes bounded pieces to caller-owned files. It preserves all holdings and original metadata. Partial writes never become completed trials. Oversized recorded plans use a fixed private file with a separate 16 MiB limit. Full plan validation precedes calculation. Existing Jobs can own a temporary completed copy, byte reservations and pinned readers. Expiry ends new access; open readers keep their bytes until closure.

Explicit version-3 operations copy complete evidence into the existing queue and saved-library databases. Each record owns ordered 64 KiB chunks. One transaction validates and publishes every byte and the original settings and labels. A failed copy preserves the source and earlier records. Opening creates a charged temporary reader and closes the database before returning it. Deleting the stored record cannot invalidate that reader. The library and the queue each keep a 100-record cap. The queue also keeps Stop precedence and mutation receipts. Old version-1/2 records are not rewritten. The additive browser reader now opens version 3 through the same ResultArtifacts boundary as fresh results. New dated browser submissions use captures and bounded evidence, including built-in-only forms. Existing legacy rows retain eager execution. Existing saved formats keep their meaning. Read the bounded evidence contract and durable snapshot contract for their limits.

Financial result contract version 1 lives in evidence headers. Existing jobs and saved results gain no required fields. Dates, status strings, nulls, ordered holdings, weights and contribution values stay complete. The reducer is a reader: an edit to it keeps every saved book. A source edit does not update a running server. Read the complete financial result contract for fields and limits.

Which calendar intervals does the source support?

Original supports the 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24-month presets and custom 1–104 weeks and 1–24 months. Fixed and random planners share backtest/calendar.py. Version 1 configurations keep interval unit and count explicit. Custom controls follow the server engine capability. Direct-file pages cannot execute dated runs. This source change does not update an installed server.

Each target uses the original start date. A week has seven calendar days. Monthly targets clamp to the last day of the destination month. Fixed targets roll forward to saved sessions. Duplicate rolled targets merge. The inclusive end mark rolls back. Random trials sample one session in each nonempty nominal block. A final partial block participates when it contains a session. Empty blocks consume no random draw. Explicit trades use the same window without an interval. Daily-cache freshness binds the cache version, research content and book identity. An edit to a calendar reader does not invalidate stored books. Artifact and financial interface versions stay the same. Canonical results retain the requested calendar and resolved session dates separately. Legacy month results keep their original fields. Saved results keep original settings and labels. Canonical random CSV files identify interval unit and count. Opening or exporting a saved result does not calculate. Read the calendar API and compatibility rules for the exact contract.

What if too few stocks pass the screen?

The program uses the stocks that pass. If 80 stocks pass a top-100 request, each starts with a weight of 1/80.

A complete empty holding period holds cash at 0% until rebalance. SPY keeps its period return. Random-date summaries keep incomplete trials visible. They exclude these trials from both paired distributions.

Which financial values are used?

The original saved annual record includes market cap, enterprise value and EV/EBITDA. Additional annual statement assets supply the financial ratio filters. The US program derives EBITDA and net debt from those values. Foreign report anchors use annual EBITDA, debt, cash, basic weighted-average shares and native fiscal closes.

Estimated EV equals estimated market cap plus report net debt. The three-year metric uses mean EBITDA from three consecutive annual reports. Missing years exclude the stock from that metric.

The US 90-day delay and foreign fallback delays are availability assumptions, not verified filing dates. Supplier data can include later revisions.

04 / Groups, filters and counts

Three choices. Three different jobs.

The stock group sets where to look. Filters set which stocks can pass. The stock count sets how many to take.

The stock group / Pool

Where should the program look?

Recorded original candidate set: restored US work retains the original 250-name screen and report-size rules. New forms offer the broader pool only.

All stocks with cached prices: a broader saved-price group. It is still a partial market universe.

Filters and stock count

Which stocks, and how many?

Filters: each Filter step searches one list of size and listing fields, EV/EBITDA metrics, built-in values, saved variables and financial inputs. It then takes a comparison and a value. Sector and exchange take Is or Is not and one choice. Filters before a Rank narrow what it ranks. Filters after the last Rank test that shortlist. Use two filters on one item to set a range.

Count: each Rank step has an inclusive rank range, such as 1–50, 1–100 or 20–40. A wider range does not expand the original 250-name screen.

Explore a setting change · Filter-first examples only

Use the broader saved-price group. Apply your filters, rank the matching stocks, then take up to 50 stocks. Saved books use reusable entry sheets, even when the exit changes.

Available conditions include market cap, enterprise value, both EV/EBITDA multiples, EBITDA/EV yield, trailing 1-year and 3-year returns, and the financial ratios below. Values use the units in each label: millions of dollars, percent, or multiples. Enter 10 for 10%. Numeric Filters offer more than (>), less than (<), at least (≥) and at most (≤). Sector and exchange Filters use is (=) or is not (≠). Use one is-not Filter for each sector that you exclude. Use two Filters on the same item for a range.

Trailing returns use dividend-adjusted closes on or before the screen date and its calendar anniversary. Each endpoint must be within seven calendar days. A leap-day anniversary clamps to 28 February. No future holding return is used. A missing value fails only a condition that needs it. A Rank leaves out stocks with a missing value. Latest, custom and random views share these rules.

Step order is shared by latest, fixed and random-date views. Filters → Rank ranks only stocks that pass the filters; older records call this filter-first. Rank → Filters takes the requested ranks from the prepared stock group, then tests the filters on that shortlist; older records call this rank-first. No replacements are added. If 20 stocks pass a top-50 shortlist, each receives 5% weight. Ranks can have gaps and keep their original numbers in stock lists and CSV files. A 10–20 Rank followed by filters tests only those original 11 ranks. Prepared pool restrictions still apply first.

Saved and queued tests keep their submitted strategy. Copying an older record restores its order as steps. Opening a record does not rewrite or recalculate it. The step builder is in current source. Source publication and an offline rebuild are needed before it appears in the installed website.

The saved books include these filter values. Changing steps reuses the books. Source or input changes require offline preparation and a website rebuild. Reload an open page to use the new build.

Financial ratios use annual statement inputs.

Choose Manage backtest data → Update data. This saves full provider responses for annual income statements, balance sheets, cash flow statements, key metrics and ratios for the chosen stock group. Every returned field is kept, including nulls, other currencies and filing metadata. US calculations retain their eligible USD inputs. Foreign calculations convert eligible report amounts at context-date FX. The raw cache keeps fields for future metric calculations. Multiple records can have the same fiscal date. The raw cache keeps every returned row. For each numerical input, matching values can be used. Conflicting values stay unavailable. Response order does not select a revision. Preparation is automatic. Reload the strategy page when the update is ready. Missing inputs exclude a stock only when a condition needs them.

P/E is screen-date market cap divided by annual net income. P/S uses annual revenue. P/B uses annual stockholders’ equity. Free cash flow is shown in millions of USD. Its yield is free cash flow divided by screen-date market cap, in percent. Price/free cash flow uses the inverse ratio. Net profit margin is net income divided by revenue, in percent.

Dividend yield is the common dividends paid in the selected annual report divided by screen-date market cap, in percent. A company that paid no dividend shows 0. Turnover rate — 1-week average is the mean saved trading volume in the 7 calendar days that end on the screen date, divided by the weighted-average share count in the selected annual report, in percent. A day without a saved volume is left out. A day with zero volume counts.

ROE uses net income divided by average stockholders’ equity from the selected and previous fiscal years, in percent. Both equity values must be positive. Current ratio is current assets divided by current liabilities. Interest coverage is EBIT divided by interest expense. Debt/equity is total debt divided by stockholders’ equity.

PEG is screen-date P/E divided by three-year diluted EPS compound annual growth, in percentage points. It needs positive diluted EPS in four consecutive fiscal years and positive growth. No analyst forecasts are used. Ratio denominators must be positive. Missing or invalid ratios stay absent. Negative cash flow and profit margins remain valid filter values.

Valuation averages: P/E, P/S and P/B each have a 3-year and a 5-year average. On each priced day, the program divides the net income, revenue or equity of the report that a book selects on that day by the market cap of that day. A loss stays negative. The average multiple is 1 divided by the mean of these daily yields. The mean uses the priced days after the calendar anniversary, through the screen date. A leap-day anniversary clamps to 28 February. An average needs a yield on or before the anniversary and a positive mean. P/E vs its 3-year average divides the current P/E by that average, and the other relatives do the same. A value below 1 means that the stock is cheaper than its usual multiple. A stock in the original group uses the same history with its own current multiples.

Sales-based operating yield spread: multiply selected annual sales by the simple average of operating margins from three consecutive fiscal years. Divide by screen-date EV. Each annual operating margin is operating income divided by revenue. Subtract the latest saved US 10-year Treasury yield on or before the screen date. Enter 5 for a spread of 5 percentage points. Revenue and EV must be positive. Margins and spreads can be negative. Missing years or Treasury values fail only this condition. Latest and dated books use their own screening sessions for the Treasury yield, even when the buy price is delayed. This filter is in current source. The installed runtime needs source publication and an offline rebuild before the filter appears.

All annual inputs match the selected report date. The market’s reporting delay, strict availability rule and 800-day current-report limit apply. A newer report cannot fill missing fields in an older report. Supplier revisions and EPS split treatment can affect results. The existing EBITDA-based stock groups remain the starting universe.

The controls above explain the architecture. They do not select real stocks or run a backtest.

05 / What gets reused

A new setting is not always a new book.

The dated engine saves compact entry sheets. Each entry and stock group has one sheet. Your final filters and ranks use its prepared values. Different exits reuse the same sheet.

Current source · Requested-pool preparation
Your changeWhat the program does
Top 50 → Top 100Reuse the same dated books. Select a wider rank range.
Change an existing filterReuse the books. Filter and rank the saved records again.
Choose the other EBITDA metricReuse the books. Both supported metrics are already prepared.
Choose the other stock groupReuse that group if it is complete. Otherwise prepare its records for the same dates. Keep the first group’s records.
Use a new entry or exitBuild a missing entry sheet on demand. Reuse it for another exit; close selected holdings in the run.
Run a new seedGenerate new trade dates. Build entry sheets that are not saved; reuse shared entries across exits.
Change source data or calculation codeRefresh the affected caches. Rebuild the saved website when needed.
How do I update my backtest data?

Open Manage backtest data, choose the market, then select Update data. The app finds missing inputs and checks for newer company reports and prices. It prepares both databases and the website automatically. You do not need to choose separate download, refresh and rebuild steps. Saved backtests and queue records keep their recorded values.

Update data→Follow progress→Ready for backtests→Open strategy page

The main card shows overall completion, Elapsed time and Estimated time remaining. The estimate includes preparation and final readiness checks. It reaches 100 only when the update succeeds and the data is ready. Estimates use the stage durations of the last successful update with the same scope, excluding the end date, scaled by live stage counts. Slower current progress can revise the estimate. Without a matching success, the card shows Estimating time remaining. Elapsed time and verified step counts and percentages remain visible. Individual stock messages stay in Details.

Closing or reloading the page does not stop the operation. Reopening shows the same work and elapsed time. The page checks for updates from other tabs and reconnects automatically. A disconnected card shows Cannot read update status and marks its progress and estimates as Last seen. A lost response to the Update button is followed by a status check. The browser does not automatically submit another update.

Select Stop update to stop new requests. Stopping safely stays visible until active workers finish. Completed work is kept. After interruption, Continue update restores the saved scope and date and reruns unfinished stages. A due, unfinished report stage is checked again even when a receipt exists. A receipt proves saved content, not the absence of a newer report. A completed stage can be reused while its content-bound receipts still apply. If only preparation remains, downloads are reused unless managed reports have become due. Verified running time excludes time while stopped or powered off.

The main Update data action maintains saved stocks, pending additions, new listings and newly eligible companies. Existing price receipts identify a managed stock even when its price file was lost. The missing file inherits no completion evidence. New companies receive price histories from 1995 and annual financial inputs. Pending additions survive interruption. Annual key metrics refresh across the due US set. US statements and ratios cover managed stocks within that set. Every returned key-metric response is retained, including companies without saved prices. New fiscal dates enter ordinary preparation under their market reporting policy. Existing valuation reports keep their saved values. Full annual input variants retain the ordinary conflict rules.

More options selects stocks and price-history dates for Update selected stocks and history. This action also prepares its data automatically. The main button updates the selected market independently of the advanced stock and date controls. Details contains local checks, report export, logs and Prepare saved data (offline). Local checks report actual dates, missing financial symbols and empty histories. Neither checking nor offline preparation needs an API key. Opening the page never starts downloads. Data actions use the backtest website’s same-origin policy at /api/data/*. Remote clients can use the same Windows Tailscale address as the strategy builder. The key stays on this computer.

Updates resume known unfinished windows and recheck a seven-day overlap in prices and Treasury yields. Checked empty histories reuse old windows. A changed adjusted price needs a consistent replacement of the full saved history. The replacement retains saved and newly returned dates, with recent prices unchanged. An incomplete or unstable replacement keeps the old file. Unchanged assets keep their bytes and timestamps. Recent overlap checks do not audit every old provider correction. Legacy gaps inside an existing span are not repaired automatically. Updates use ordinary preparation. Full historical precomputation belongs in that flow. Its sheets stage runs after website output and before verification; the scheduler owns no sheet rules.

One small atomic record at data/data-refresh.json stores state, scope, target date, current stage, stage counts, a successful stage prefix, verified active seconds, pending additions, last success and previous successful stage durations. The existing financial cache owner publishes both status and inputs. There is no separate update owner or per-stock work record. Status reads do not resume or write work. A saved running state becomes interrupted when the cache is free. A foreign busy cache leaves it unconfirmed: that owner could be a backtest. The page does not claim an update is still running or offer Stop for that unidentified owner. A successful empty response does not advance market coverage. Partial updates can prepare valid saved inputs, but remain visibly partial. Readiness and update success stay separate.

The downloader uses up to 32 parallel requests. It reuses HTTP connections. Compressed responses reduce transferred bytes. The transport requests gzip compression and decodes it before checking the data. Plain responses also work. A shared gate permits at most 45 request starts per second by default. This is 2,700 starts per minute, below this account’s stated allowance of 3,000 calls per minute. A 429 response pauses all workers and lowers the start rate. Retries are bounded and cancellation stops new requests. One owner saves each completed result. Stock and SPY windows cover up to ten years. Treasury windows remain monthly.

Zero or negative adjusted prices are skipped. Usable prices are saved and the batch continues. Skipped dates remain unavailable. The panel warns you and the exported check report lists those dates. These exclusions stay in the content-bound receipt, so later checks still show them. A completed window does not guarantee a price on each date. A response with only excluded prices is recorded as checked but unavailable. It stores no invented prices and does not stop the batch. Missing or nonfinite values still fail. Malformed rows, duplicate usable dates and dates outside the requested window also fail. The error names the affected file and date window.

Successful requests, including empty responses, are recorded in raw/download-coverage.json. Each entry is tied to the saved file by a content hash. Receipts also retain the original saved span and one previous generation. Interrupted publication can match either exact file generation without losing known unfinished windows. Retry reuses a completed window only while that file remains valid and unchanged. Missing or damaged files lose that completion evidence. They can be downloaded again. Legacy entries without a hash do not prove completion. Actual price dates remain visible. A checked range does not guarantee every session. Short histories can come from IPOs or trading stops. Legacy gaps inside an existing span are not repaired automatically. Managed downloads retain their original saved span and each completed window. A late result cannot hide an unfinished earlier window.

Each financial append ends with a newline and is flushed to disk. Before the next owned append or preparation, cleanup removes only an incomplete, unparseable final line. A complete valid JSON tail without a newline is retained. Earlier bytes are not rewritten by this cleanup. Read-only inspectors retain the ordinary reader. Main's existing repair and archive behavior for malformed complete records stays available. Atomic cache replacement flushes its file before rename and synchronizes the directory on POSIX. Python exposes no portable equivalent directory synchronization on Windows. Physical power-cut behavior is not established by these private tests.

Research preparation reuses current data or reconciles changed typed rows in one transaction. The last step of that transaction folds the valuation sums. Cold, schema or fact-code builds use a complete replacement. Failure keeps the previous committed data. Daily repairs commit per sheet and publish the new binding last. Before a website rebuild changes output, it removes the old completion marker and synchronizes that directory. It flushes all output files before publishing the completion marker last. Freshness requires the marker, matching input identity and the output files. The server builds in process under cache ownership, so a killed parent cannot leave an unowned build child. Open the strategy page after completion to load the prepared data.

Every managed refresh updates company lists, prices, SPY, Treasury and FX for its markets. This includes the 07:00 Hong Kong cycle for markets with saved inventories, and managed data-panel updates. It checks reports when the Hong Kong date is Saturday and that day has not been checked, or when the last successful report check is more than seven days old. A missing check is due immediately. Reports cover listed companies and pending additions. A due check includes delisted companies when the full sweep is missing or more than 90 days old. Custom-scoped updates and the separate Download action keep their full report behavior. The existing status record keeps last_report_check and last_full_sweep. Managed refreshes use these dates. Only an all-markets managed run advances them, after its download phase finishes with no report failures. A Stop or exception during downloads keeps the old dates. A recorded price failure does not prevent this advance. Single-market updates preserve both dates. Managed Continue recalculates the schedule on its current Hong Kong date. If a full sweep becomes due, it checks completed report stages again for delisted companies. Skipped stages show Reports: next check Saturday and add no estimated time. Skipped runs retain the previous measured report durations for the next due run. The already authorized 07:00 cycle can run independently of the manual Continue button. A missed schedule waits until the next day. Ordinary startup remains offline and can prepare valid saved inputs. Source ownership precedes the existing financial process lock, financial file lock, connections and workers. Financial ownership ends only after worker completion and database closure. Nested preparation reuses it. Terminal shutdown waits for cleanup. Atomic publication retains the bounded Windows sharing-lock retries.

The panel is served directly from source at /data.html. Missing essential raw data opens this recovery panel, which needs no prepared database or prior website build. A saved HTML copy needs the local service. Logs stay under Details and data/logs/. They exclude keys, provider URLs and response bodies. Source checks do not establish installed readiness or real-cache coverage.

Which download settings were measured?

The 22 October 2026 experiment used native Windows Python 3.12 and uncached dividend-adjusted stock histories. The temporary experiment did not change the active raw cache. For 16 one-year requests, one pooled worker took 22.09–31.81 seconds. Four workers took 5.57–6.84 seconds. Eight took 3.04–3.54 seconds. Sixteen took 4.06 seconds in one round. These transport tests had no steady start-rate cap.

The policy selected on 22 October had eight workers and a four-starts-per-second cap. It saved 16 one-year histories in 6.56 seconds with 16 HTTP 200 responses and no retries. The serial reference took 42.47 seconds. These runs used the same stock symbols but different historical years. They are samples, not a controlled same-period speedup or a universal optimum.

The experiment also found a Python 3.12 response-reuse problem. The transport now closes each exhausted response before the next request. The empty Treasury probe did not establish annual Treasury coverage, so monthly windows remain. Read the 22 October settings and measurements for that evidence.

The 23 October standalone transport experiment made 1,392 distinct stock/window requests. All returned HTTP 200. Across compressed cases, gzip reduced transferred body bytes by 89.1%. Native Windows Python 3.12.1 averaged 207 calls per minute with eight workers and four starts per second. It averaged 1,207 calls per minute with 32 workers and 45 starts per second, without compression. A larger gzip batch on WSL Python 3.14.4 averaged 2,265 calls per minute with 32 workers. The higher worker counts tested were slower.

That experiment supports the current 32-worker, 45-starts-per-second policy with gzip. Its fresh-pool batches lasted about 2–19 seconds. They used different stocks, historical periods and environments. These are prior transport measurements. They are not new application tests, a controlled application speedup, a sustained-rate test or guaranteed throughput. The full data-panel publication path was not measured. Read the 23 October settings and measurements for the scope and limits.

The source now contains the new transport settings. Restart an existing local server to load the current Python code. Reload the data panel to see the current text. Implementation checks use local provider fixtures and temporary caches. They do not download market data.

↻

Replay can be fast because the work is already saved.

In the reference Windows test, 100 fresh trials took 467 seconds. A replay of those saved books took 5.7 seconds. These are different jobs.

Which entry sheets does an update keep?

A sheet contains entry information for one stock group and one saved market session. It has no holding exit or future return. Each stock occupies one compact row. Missing metric pairs or filter values stay unavailable. Stored owner numbers keep their existing REAL rounding and zero normalization. Typed research facts and formula outputs keep signed zero.

Compatible research changes repair only affected company rows in historical cached sheets. US statement changes refresh candidate counts and ranks from statements alone. Affected legacy pools rebuild on demand. Removed sessions lose their sheets. Each repair commits separately. Latest rebuilds before the new binding commits last. An interruption leaves the old binding, so readers refuse partial work and a retry repeats the repair. Changed book code or an unmatched research base resets the disposable cache. An older or foreign cache also rebuilds. Locked files and I/O errors stop preparation without replacing the file. Research failure keeps its previous committed data.

Unchanged identities retain historical sheets. An edit to a reader or custom formula does not rebuild them. The latest screen keeps its own listed-company and exact-session rule. Historical sheets allow entry up to four calendar days later. Before either ranking order or formula evaluation, the run removes actual entries on or after exit. It then calls books.close only for selected holdings, preserving scheduled exits, last available prices and bankruptcy windows. Missing close evidence fails explicitly. SPY returns use the same admitted research generation.

Unified Update data and 07:00 Hong Kong maintenance fill missing cached historical entries from 1 January 1996 through each market’s latest saved session. Empty sheets count as complete. Legacy stays on demand. The sheets stage follows website publication and precedes verification. Plain startup, CLI preparation and runs keep on-demand behavior. Historical coverage adds no readiness state and does not block website publication, which embeds latest only. Source checks and bench parity remain separate from installed readiness. The daily maintenance time remains 07:00 Hong Kong.

book_batch.precompute reuses the existing read-only workers and parent writer. One complete sheet commits at a time. Continue builds only missing historical cached completion rows under the admitted binding. Latest-policy headers do not count; empty completions do. Existing progress starts at retained/total sheets and advances after each commit. Stage durations include this work; missing prior timing keeps estimates unknown. Cancellation retains earlier commits and joins workers before releasing cache ownership. No table, checkpoint format or VACUUM is added.

What happens if I stop a run?

A fixed-date request saves its new books together. A random batch calculates missing books in parallel. It saves all new books for one trial together, in trial order.

Workers only read data. One parent process saves results in SQLite. If worker processes evaluate the trials, a stop waits until the trials in progress end. A failed trial leaves no partial new books. Unfinished writes roll back. Previously saved books remain. The queue runs an interrupted test again with the same seed. Completed books can be reused. A stopped test does not resume by itself.

06 / Why new trials take time

Plan shared work.
Calculate books in parallel.

The earlier engine prepared both stock groups for every new date pair. Original prepares only the requested group. Its random batches plan unique missing books upfront. Worker processes calculate ahead. One writer saves each complete trial. Each entry sheet gets both supported metrics. The run calculates holding returns only after selection.

A random-date strategy test can have all its books saved. If it has at least two trials and at least 96 periods, up to six worker processes then evaluate its trials. The result is the same as the result of a one-process run. A smaller test, or a test with a missing book, evaluates its trials in one process.

The website runs only Original. The source has no experimental (Numba) engine. The compiled-backtest and parallel-backtest plan summaries keep its measurements.

Earlier engine / Benchmark reference

New dates→Original groupBroader group→Select stocks

The earlier engine prepared the broader group for an original-group request. New trials created many extra records.

Requested pool and parallel books / In current source

New dates→Requested group only→Parallel books→One writer

Prepare only the group you chose. Plan each missing entry/pool sheet once. Calculate sheets with read-only workers. Save complete trials through one SQLite writer. An empty group also counts as complete.

Test: original candidate set, top 50, annual random rebalances, 1996–2026. The end date was 20 October 2026. Seed: 20261022. Loading and per-trial saving are included. Common test-only cloning is excluded. The OS file cache was not cleared.

The Windows worker comparison took 103.4, 62.0, 40.9 and 33.2 seconds with 1, 2, 4 and 8 workers. A fresh serial requested-group control took 133.3 seconds. A four-worker check of the applied code took 43.2 seconds, including worker shutdown cleanup. Saved-book replays took about 5.6 seconds. The current default is eight workers for 16 or more missing books, and each worker decodes a company’s financial inputs once. These timings do not measure that default.

All selected holdings, prices, returns and exit statuses matched exactly. The measured gain applies to the original group. Selecting the broader group avoids much less work. Top 100 and P/B-filtered runs were not benchmarked.

Why fewer records help.
The reference test prepared 4,010,439 stock records. The requested-group test prepared 537,906. These are records across periods, not unique companies.

Why shared data is optional.
It added about 12.6 seconds of loading in the 100-trial test. At 24 trials, group-only took 32 seconds. The combined version took 35 seconds.

How are tests that name the experimental engine handled?

The source has no experimental (Numba) engine. The website runs only Original. A new draft shows no engine choice. The server refuses a request that names the experimental engine. A restored test that names it keeps that engine and shows the engine choice. Choose Original to run it. A waiting queued test that names it stays waiting. Edit it to choose Original, or delete it. Manage backtest data has no experimental preparation action. Saved results from the experimental engine open, compare and export with their producer label. Leftover data/numerical/ files on the runtime are unused. The experiment summaries record its decisions and measurements.

All calculation routes share one ordinary admission owner. Callers no longer prehold financial ownership. It acquires financial ownership, checks readiness, calculates and closes the database before releasing ownership. Queue waits remain cancellable. Only admission contention is retried. Random jobs and queued results retain every trial holding. Shutdown signals the queue before it closes calculation admission. Interrupted queue work returns to waiting. An explicit Stop stays cancelled. Application owners then join. Late request bodies cannot begin calculation. Stored results and held edits remain available without calculation.

Freshness inventory checked 31 October 2026. Every validation still checks the current saved inputs at the same points. Fresh directory entries supply metadata for the same selected files. Paths, case and link rules, sizes, timestamps and directory markers retain their meanings. The signature holds no report cutoff. No inventory is reused by another check. Within one check, financial files in the same folder share its checked relative-path prefix. Exact folder spelling and file names remain in the saved keys. These prefixes expire with the check. A missing discovered asset still fails validation. A source change still requires ordinary preparation.

The research record holds the price-file inventory that its preparation accepted. Editing an existing price file can leave its directory timestamp unchanged. After research preparation accepts that edit, the old daily cache is stale. Daily preparation then updates the book cache. Normal daily checks read committed inventory metadata. They do not scan every raw price file. Older daily caches start empty. Saved user snapshots stay independent. Missing or mismatched evidence fails validation. Historical receipts keep their original identities.

Which website functions use Original?

Latest picks use shared prepared data in the browser. Other latest chains use Original on the local service. Fixed and random custom-date runs and variable strategies use Original. Original supports custom weeks and months, both stock pools, both selection orders and the full current metric and filter catalog.

How do complete evidence results open and download?

Evidence-backed results keep their original settings, labels and every selected stock. Fresh results, library records and queue records use one ResultArtifacts reader. Opening these stored bytes needs no current financial generation, readiness check or calculation. Old version-1/2 records still open without being rewritten; a version-1/2 January record opens in the dated view. Every dated test starts from Add to queue. Every new dated submission captures one chain of steps and uses bounded evidence. Built-in sources read precomputed sheet values. The offline latest screen runs filters it supports and one highest EBITDA/EV-yield Rank, first or last. Screen latest runs every other chain on the service, from the open book of exact-session prices for listed companies. That result shows the market's latest cached session. Existing waiting and held queue rows keep their request format and execution. Saving an unchanged held edit keeps its original request in any format. Name-only held edits preserve the seed and plan. A changed edit and a copy capture a chain. StrategyDraft has one restore path for flat settings, capture/1 and capture/2. Old bounds become Filter steps on size fields, sector, exchange and the ranked metric's yield and multiple. A zero minimum adds no step. Stored metric pairs are complete or absent, so ranking the yield lane alone is exact. Old captures keep their original meaning. An empty legacy minimum cap, EV or yield returns as a Filter without a value, and submission asks for one. A copy that needs more than 50 steps is refused. Stored records are never rewritten. Trial inspection reads the stored rows and calculates nothing. A capture allows 192 KiB. Settings, request wrappers and display metadata together allow 256 KiB. Recorded plans have a separate 16 MiB allowance. The run endpoint keeps its 16 MiB whole-body transport limit. The queue keeps its 256 KiB whole-body limit.

The period and stock tables retain one page each. Next and Previous controls reach every period and stock. The chart states which period range it shows. Every random trial remains selectable, including incomplete trials. Open Stock return contributions to read all original selected stocks in two ordered passes. They retain totals and the top ten stocks. Changing the table page cannot change attribution.

Downloads contain the complete selected trial, even when its table shows one page. The service sends UTF-8 CSV attachments in bounded chunks. Columns, order, quoting, CRLF separators, numeric spelling and filenames match eager downloads. An interrupted attachment cannot satisfy its complete Content-Length. The browser does not collect all holdings into a CSV Blob.

Existing ResultAccess owns acquired display lifetimes separately from Jobs and calculation runs. It admits up to 16 displays and 32 active requests. Each request gets an independent stream. Deleting the stored source or expiring its job ends new acquisition. An existing display and an active export keep their original bytes. Replacing a view releases its display; active exports keep their own pins. Late replies must match the artifact and current selection. A held StrategyDraft refuses replacement before a result is published.

Inline saved and queue results have one 128 MiB save and open limit. It includes the complete JSON response and its record metadata. A library save or queue move above that limit fails before publication. The queue keeps the completed result visible as Completed — waiting to save. It shows the 128 MiB limit reason. This transfer does not retry automatically. Existing records keep their stored bytes.

Page targets are 64 rows and 256 KiB. One codec-valid record can exceed that target. Paged evidence responses retain their separate 32 MiB bound. One UTF-8 JSON serializer measures and sends the same bytes. Valid Unicode records do not grow through ASCII escaping. These are encoded-data and admission limits. They do not establish hardware RAM exhaustion, browser-memory containment or disk quotas. A failed browser-departure release can leave an orphan until service shutdown. No displayed result is silently evicted.

Opening first validates the complete result. That pass builds a compact directory of trial summary locations and period sizes. Summary cards then read the selected summary directly, without decoding its holdings or earlier trials. The directory retains no stock rows and changes no saved format. It ends with the acquired reader. Each request opens an independent stream. Requests, summary reads and record traversals check the complete file identity, including unread data. Framing, checksums, cancellation and ordinary record validation stay in force. Period and holding pages still scan sequentially.

The table and both attribution passes share the first stock page. A top-50 period needs one stock-page request. Each pass reads later pages when needed. Downloads read the trial summary directly, then count and stream exact CSV bytes in separate bounded passes.

What did the complete fictional website check prove?

The benchmark-only source-service check is not in the current source. Its fictional source-root fixture remains in tests/source_service_fixture.py for current preparation, engine and browser tests. The check starts with 64 fictional companies. Its weekday calendar runs from 1992 to 21 October 2026. The copied source of that time prepared the January and daily databases, and the independent engine agreed on all 31 baseline books and their 50 holdings. The ordinary builder created the page and exports. It does not use prepared-table substitutes or a placeholder page.

The check uses the real latest, historical, fixed-date and random-date controls. Browser downloads must match SQL or ordinary HTTP results. It checks saved-date inspection, reload and replay, empty selections, data inspection and rebuild. A saved-input edit must reject stale requests. A latest-only price update must keep historical results. A private missing-key path keeps the real key untouched. No market-data download runs.

The service owns copied source before application imports. It releases source after data jobs, request threads and its listener close. Page and panel delivery remain available during a saved-data rebuild. Financial requests wait for ordinary cache ownership to end. Cooperative observation yields to arriving work. These are separate behaviors; this does not prove zero-delay access.

This fixture has separate storage and service allowances. Size checks are not disk quotas. Its cold databases exceed the older 32 MiB capture fixture allowance. That older allowance does not change. That earlier source-service check did not qualify combined attachment. The later combined-service check qualifies its separately declared fictional workload. The Linux browser checks the WSL service. Native HTTP checks pass. That check used a Linux browser. A later private native-browser check also passes on the same fictional source fixture. It compares six scenario groups and seven saved CSV files with SQL and ordinary function results. The check does not qualify real-data capacity, installed compatibility, browser resources or full isolation. Real admission stays closed.

What does the private native-browser check prove?

An existing Windows Chrome browser uses a new private profile. A test-only owner starts it inside the existing Windows Job before application work begins. It connects only to the debugger address recorded by that profile. It does not attach to an existing browser or use the installed website.

The check uses real pointer clicks and ordinary control events. It saves each CSV through the browser. Download events, file bytes and hashes establish each completed download. Latest, historical, fixed-date and random-date results agree with the fictional fixture’s SQL and ordinary function evidence. The mobile main page and data panel have no horizontal overflow. Check and Rebuild use saved fictional inputs.

Browser shutdown confirms that descendants, streams and Job handles close before either private root is removed. Unknown closure retains owners for retry. Logical storage checks are not disk quotas. Job commit, process, CPU-share and periodic user-time limits do not prove total residency, hard thread limits, hard I/O or complete isolation. This check gives no new performance result and opens no real admission.

Source code and a running server can differ.

The requested-pool change is now in the source. Upfront planning and parallel book calculation are also applied. Eight workers are the automatic default for batches with at least 16 missing books; each worker decodes a company's financial inputs once. Small batches stay serial. Shared in-memory data was only a benchmark prototype. That prototype was later removed. Normal backtest-web.cmd starts retain the installed revision. Use an explicit WSL revision command only when a deliberate source update is authorized.

Research preparationbacktest/inputs/research.py
data/research.sqlite		Prepares companies with their listing, annual reports and typed facts. It holds no book. Compatible builds reconcile changed rows in one transaction and skip decoding unchanged price and annual files. The last step folds the valuation sums. A cold build folds every company. A compatible build refolds each affected company once, from its earliest sheet cutoff over all markets, with the current market of the company. The sums add in date order from zero, so a refold gives the same bits as a cold build. Cold, schema or fact-code builds use a temporary file and atomic replacement. A cold build of 2,000 or more companies uses eight worker processes. Each worker builds one range of symbols in its own temporary file beside the database. The parent process copies the rows and sums of each company into its one transaction, so the database is the same as a one-process build. A Stop or a failure stops the workers and removes their files. If the parent process is killed, the workers end and the next build removes the files. Failure keeps the previous committed data. An unreadable saved file stops preparation. Its metadata table is the one research record: the schema version, the raw-file signature, each price file’s stamps and the identity. The identity holds latest dates by market, the legacy US latest date, the content digest of the fact-row code and the content identity of the facts, from the bytes of every saved file read. code_sources(role) is the one rule of code roles. The research identity binds the fact-row code, so an edit to it rebuilds research. The book identity binds the book code. Readers bind no identity. A rewrite with equal bytes keeps both identities.
