Where is the Git history in this workspace?

The authoritative source checkout is in WSL. Its .git file points to the preserved .git-local/ history. Ordinary Git commands work there. The native Windows runtime is a deployed export. It has no separate repository.

The retained original Windows folder has an empty, read-only .git/ folder. In that folder, use git --git-dir=.git-local --work-tree=. status. Use the same options for log and diff. Make edits and commits only in the WSL source checkout. If the default Git wrapper fails with a WSL socket error, use /usr/bin/git. Keep the existing history.

How are inputs separate from calculation?

Saved inputs and daily storage live in backtest/inputs/. The Original engine reads that storage and calculates missing books. The independent reference keeps its own screening and return arithmetic.

backtest/financial/books.py calculates entry valuation without an exit date. A dated holding adds the exit price, return and status (books.close). Unknown source structures fail explicitly.

What dated observations are available for custom variables?

The source preserves why all 53 direct annual inputs are available or missing. Income, balance-sheet and cash-flow fields keep their endpoint and exact fiscal date. Equal values with matching report currencies agree. Conflicting values stay unavailable. A null does not replace a known value. A newer report with missing fields stays visible. A reader cannot skip it to find a more complete report.

Each source row identifies the saved file bytes by digest and disposition. Damaged assets can retain usable rows. Their content hash identifies the source; it does not prove a completed download. Raw responses stay unchanged.

The research database holds these typed facts beside the statements. A latest root is admitted by the latest book’s rule: admitted or the denial reason, the candidate rank, the report dates and the valuation. Admission uses cached listing status and the exact latest session of the selected market. A denial reason is distinct from a missing input. This admission does not establish listing status at an earlier date.

Resolve saved inputs→Write typed facts→Bind them in the daily cache→Borrow one view per operation

backtest/inputs/facts.py owns the typed tables and the book facts port. backtest/inputs/fact_view.py owns the borrowed view. backtest/inputs/financial_inputs.py keeps one shared annual resolver. Its existing values-only interface returns the same values. Value columns have no declared type, so a signed zero survives. A new research schema or daily cache version makes older caches rebuild. The schema version and the content identity of the facts and of the fact-row code bind reuse. Missing or stale facts require offline preparation.

A borrowed view uses the operation’s one daily connection and reads the facts through its attached research schema. It adds no worker or lock. Close the view before the connection. It reads each company, day and source once. Returned price observations include their actual dates.

backtest/variables/columns.py directly supplies all 57 inputs plus operating margin and existing dated enterprise value. Amounts use USD. Annual weighted-average share counts use shares. Catalog /4 applies market-aware conversion and report timing. Typed formulas offer each /4 input once by a plain name. The preserved four-item catalog serves legacy definitions. Formulas can use the complete /1 and /2 vocabulary and the /3 measure adapters. Original execution accepts captured /1, /2, /3 and /4 programs. Foreign execution requires /4. A margin uses a fraction, so 12% is 0.12. An annual history returns separate fiscal members, oldest first. It calculates no average or formula.

facts.resolve resolves saved stock, Treasury and SPY calendar rows separately from legacy financial normalization. Missing receipts do not erase usable facts or prove completed downloads. Download receipts are not a preparation input. A receipt change alone does not make prepared data stale.

Price and volume use the selected market’s saved session on or before the context, within seven calendar days. Each field needs the stock’s own row at that exact session. Price must be finite and positive. Volume can be zero or fractional and remains usable without price. Price uses USD/share in the admitted USD company context when route currency is absent. Catalogs /1–/3 retain identity conversion and reject foreign contexts. Catalog /4 converts foreign prices to USD using the previous completed FX fixing.

Treasury inputs use the latest saved source date on or before a US context, strictly before an Asian context. Each field resolves at that date. A null, invalid or conflicting field stays unavailable even when an older value exists. Signed and zero rates remain valid. Provider percent is divided by 100. These dated inputs need no annual anchor after root admission. Their rules do not change existing financial lookups.

The legacy top-250 buffer is formed before checking cached prices. Earlier dates keep the root membership and candidate rank.

Admit the original root→Resolve the dated context→Return values and evidence

At each context date, reports must be known strictly before that date. The selected report can be at most 800 days old. Older annual history members do not inherit that age limit. One income fiscal spine selects periods before any endpoint join. The current period is the existing financial-policy anchor. Each earlier calendar year uses its latest eligible income date. Every endpoint joins that exact date. A missing selected-report field stays missing. A missing middle year makes the requested history unavailable. Enterprise value uses the existing price lookup rules and needs no exit price.

Malformed roots, future dates and unsupported inputs fail before observation work. Each endpoint history keeps its 16,384-row bound. Indexed row reads check view lifetime. The freshness check runs at admission and between operation steps. Boolean, malformed and nonfinite new fields stay unavailable. Finite signed amounts and zero stay valid. Raw acceptance and legacy financial values keep their existing rules. Missing data retains a reason. Cancellation, stale inputs or a closed attachment fail the complete operation. Returned evidence remains readable after closure. The shared variable workspace uses these inputs beside the standalone built-ins. The installed server and native-cache coverage remain outside these fixture checks.

What formulas can current source evaluate?

The source provides one formula evaluator, backtest/variables/columns.py. It returns one scalar value for each admitted company, date and captured formula, or an explanation of that value. The shared variable workspace uses this owner beside the standalone built-ins. Original is the only engine the website runs. It also provides a separate durable variable library. These capabilities are integrated into main.

Formulas use all 57 inputs and the two adapters, constants, ordered arithmetic, annual mean/min/max, dated contexts and immutable references. Definition version 2 also supports annual growth and CAGR over complete consecutive observations. Application formulas accept definition versions 1–3 and catalogs /1–/4. Catalogs /1–/3 keep US semantics. A three-year mean uses three annual members. Growth and CAGR use one fewer interval than annual members. A calendar lookback changes the date of the whole subtree. It is not a quarterly report. Calendar statistics, quarterly accounts and TTM remain unsupported.

A separate semantic catalog describes the inputs. It describes all 57 direct inputs and the two existing operating-margin and EV adapters. Descriptions record source endpoint, field, unit, sign, sampling, history and missing-data rules. The evaluator implements all 57 direct observations and the existing margin and EV adapters. Execution accepts the expanded captured vocabulary. The editor offers each input once by a plain name, with suggestions while you type and a list by category. A catalog description does not establish company/date coverage.

Each definition keeps its recorded catalog. financial-parameters/1 retains its original four parameters and three units. financial-parameters/2 adds the complete vocabulary and the share unit. USD/share times share gives USD. Annual average shares describe a period. Volume describes one session. Neither replaces dated market-cap policy. Treasury descriptions convert provider percent to fractions. The language check, definitions.require_program, is the one formula gate. It checks every captured definition before financial work. This includes constant-only and unused definitions. The one evaluator implements the whole language: every operation, statistic and /1–/4 parameter. A guard test in tests/test_parameter_admission.py evaluates each of them. Execution restores its capture through this check. Invalid work fails before readiness or financial inputs.

The semantic source participates in current policy fingerprints. Old definitions, revisions, programs, captures, queued intent and completed scalar evidence keep their bytes and meaning. No saved definition, capture, artifact or durable format changes. Typed facts hold the annual and dated inputs. Prepared latest measure lanes are the stored latest book rows. Synthetic checks establish no native-cache coverage or installed-data change.

Capture definitions→Check language and references→Infer units→Publish immutable program

Constants use canonical units. A displayed 12% margin participates as 0.12. Decimal spelling is normalized before content hashing. Tree order and display settings remain part of the definition identity. References name exact content revisions. Missing references and cycles fail validation. No variable library is needed.

The language has fixed size and depth ceilings. Callers can lower them. A submitted decimal has at most 64 characters. Exponent expansion has a separate 1,024-byte ceiling. A checked program can retain that expanded spelling. The restore boundary reconstructs its identities, edges, units and requirements before execution can use it.

Bind company and date→Admit bounded work→Read dated observations→Return scalar and evidence

The borrowed view owns admission and entry valuation. The evaluator owns report choice, annual alignment and dated enterprise value. Even a constant requires admission. Asking for fewer companies cannot promote a stock into the legacy buffer. An earlier context keeps the original rank. A derived date stays distinct from its parent even when both dates agree.

Arithmetic uses binary64 in tree order. Mean adds annual members oldest first, then divides by their count. It starts with the oldest member. Min/max keep that member when values tie. Generic division accepts a negative nonzero denominator. Built-in ratios keep their existing denominator rules. Missing multiplied by zero stays missing. Both operand explanations remain available. Zero division and nonfinite output return an unavailable value with a reason.

Unsupported work fails before inputs are read. Contexts nest at most 32 deep. One explanation block fits one 8 MiB evidence record or is split in half. These are content bounds, not a measure of process memory. Nothing is truncated to fit.

An explanation block captures the formula, evaluator policy, generation, all dated observations and operation evidence. It remains readable after the view and its connections close. Cancellation or stale inputs abort the whole operation. Freshness is checked at each operation boundary. No result reader needs the current variable library.

backtest/variables/parameters.py owns versioned meaning and unit vocabulary. backtest/variables/definitions.py owns validation, identities and inferred dimensions. backtest/variables/columns.py owns observation rules, arithmetic and explanation blocks. One code path gives values and their explanations. These source fixtures establish no native-cache coverage or installed-server change. The separate durable variable library is described below. The shared editor connects formulas to the ordinary strategy form.

Catalog /3 has 77 parameter IDs. They include 57 direct inputs and the adapters needed by 33 named measures. The 33 measures are reusable definitions, not 33 more direct inputs. One program can contain at most 32 definitions. This evidence comes from private synthetic fixtures. It does not establish installed readiness or coverage for any company or date.

A compound input, such as Gross profit, is a named measure: the formula holds an exact reference to it. Its complete definitions and labels travel with the capture. Save and reopen resolve the exact built-in revision without importing it into My variables. A wrong revision or damaged archive fails explicitly. Detached results use their embedded content and read no current measure registry.

New formulas use definition version 3, catalog financial-parameters/4 and temporal policy market-annual/1. Opening an old formula keeps its original namespace while its text is unchanged; edited text uses the current form. Hong Kong and Japan runs use its /4 form. Annual mean, minimum and maximum require the complete consecutive history. Growth and CAGR require 2–10 observations. Quarterly, TTM and calendar-series statistics remain unsupported. Share counts retain share units.

In one private WSL qualification workload, 64 fictional companies used top 10 across 31 periods from 1996 to 2026. Preparation took 53.445 seconds. The complete Original call took 537.448 seconds. The same private native case took 771.660 seconds for Original. Other qualification work ran at the same time. This is not a claim about installed or live-cache capacity.

How does custom scalar selection work?

Custom ranking and filters select from each complete prepared scope. The shared variable workspace uses this selector beside the standalone built-ins. Each stored row of the scope is admitted: the book kept only the companies that passed the legacy top-250 buffer and the other gates.

Read the complete prepared scope→Evaluate admitted formulas→Rank and test conditions→Return survivors and evidence

Custom ranking requires Highest or Lowest. Values use finite binary64 without rounding. Negative values and zero can rank. Missing ranking values are excluded. Equal values, including signed zero, tie by original candidate rank, then symbol. Null candidate ranks come first.

Filter first applies all conditions before ranking. Rank first selects the inclusive range before conditions. It preserves original ranks and adds no replacements. Each pool, mode and date ranks independently. Survivors receive equal weights. Empty scopes remain explicit. A complete empty selection holds cash at 0% until rebalance. CAGR includes the full elapsed window.

Custom thresholds use canonical units. An input of 8% compares as 0.08. Exact decimal conversion precedes binary64 comparison. The original submitted threshold and display unit remain separate evidence. Missing values fail active conditions that need them. No hidden minimum yield applies to custom ranking. No reciprocal yield is invented.

backtest/selection.py owns pure scalar ordering and conditions. backtest/application/scalar_execution.py combines stored and formula lanes and selects once per scope. definitions.normalize_quantity() owns custom threshold conversion. Selected rows keep links to their explanation blocks. They remain readable after the view and its connections close. Cancellation or stale inputs abort the operation. The view checks freshness after each scope. When worker processes evaluate the trials, the parent process checks it while it waits for them.

A strategy allows at most 50 conditions and 8,192 candidates in a scope. No evidence is truncated.

Legacy SQL and browser adapters keep stored ranking pairs and filter values in their original comparison scale. Stored yield is not recalculated from its multiple. Existing defaults and inclusive limits stay the same. Legacy requests retain up to 50 threshold filters plus their size, yield and metadata conditions. The callable formula limit stays at 50 conditions. Legacy prepared populations do not inherit the callable candidate limit. No strategy request or saved result is rewritten.

The research input signature binds the shared selection source. A source change follows the existing preparation and rebuild rules. Unsupported experimental formula requests fail before readiness or financial execution, including raw formula aliases and unsupported execution modes. There is no silent fallback. The separate durable variable library is described below. The shared variable workspace supplies the same expression tree for ranking and conditions. Original is the only engine the website runs. These capabilities are integrated into main. Native-cache coverage remains unknown.

How are reusable variables kept?

The source provides a callable durable variable library. The shared variable workspace uses this owner beside the standalone built-ins. Each saved variable has a stable ID. Its formula revisions are immutable. Renaming or changing a favourite changes only library metadata. Changing formula content or its display convention creates a content revision. Equivalent normalized content reuses the existing revision.

Save authored formula→Resolve exact dependencies→Validate with definition owner→Commit durable revision

The library uses data/variable-library.sqlite. Keep this durable user file during cache rebuilds, cleanup and source deployment. It is separate from saved backtests, the queue and financial caches. User variables have no automatic eviction. Deleting an entry hides it from the active library. All immutable revisions and its last metadata remain retained. A surviving formula can still resolve an exact deleted revision.

Each entry has a mutable version as well as its content revision. An edit must supply the expected entry version. Two writers cannot silently replace each other's changes. A stale writer gets a conflict. SQLite commit is the publication point. A failed operation or process exit before commit preserves the previous state. Restart reads committed data. An unsupported or damaged store is kept and reported. It is never rebuilt from financial caches.

backtest/variables/definitions.py owns reference discovery, normalization, hashes, units and validation. References always name exact revisions. There is no dynamic latest reference. The library retains authored literals such as 1e100. Resolution returns the existing complete immutable formula program. Its checked restore boundary accepts canonical expanded literals without widening the rules for new submissions.

Open one library snapshot→Resolve exact program→Capture names and provenance→Close storage and return

A capture owns the complete program and one label for each definition. Definitions and labels come from one database snapshot. Concurrent edits cannot mix their states. Archived revisions use the name, entry version and deleted status at capture time. They do not use the name at original revision creation. Deleted entries use their retained final metadata. Favourite status stays a library preference.

capture_submitted() captures a complete unsaved program without opening or creating a library file. Missing submitted dependencies fail. It shares the existing capture envelope and validation. Store.capture() still requires an existing recognized store. Submission-local definitions use the same validator. Optional labels apply only to submitted definitions. A missing local label uses its full variable ID. These definitions are not saved by capture. Formula and bundle revisions exclude names and provenance. A rename can change captured labels without changing the program.

VariableCapture stores immutable canonical bytes. require_capture() checks the complete program, ordered labels, provenance and bounds without opening a library. It uses the existing program restore boundary for expanded literals. The complete capture allows at most 3 MiB of encoded content. Callers can lower that ceiling. Escaped label text counts toward the bound. Nothing is truncated. Cancellation or invalid content returns no partial capture.

The returned program and labels need no later library state. They remain valid after editing, deletion, restart or removal of the library file. Completed formula and selection explanations stay detached after input views and attachments close. All database connections close before capture returns. The library starts no worker or financial operation. It changes no source/cache ownership, cancellation or input-attachment lifetime.

The library itself adds no editor or strategy route. Strategy execution is described below. Existing queue records and saved results are not rewritten. Original is the only engine the website runs. These capabilities are integrated into main. Native-cache coverage remains unknown.

How do I create and use a variable?

The strategy is a list of steps under the stock universe. + Add filter and + Add rank add a step. Each step searches one list: size and listing fields (Filters only), EV/EBITDA metrics, built-in values, My variables and financial inputs. The EV/EBITDA metrics have two forms. A yield has the name EBITDA / EV, and a higher yield is cheaper. A multiple has the name EV / EBITDA, and a lower multiple is cheaper. The list shows this note with each form. Financial inputs lists each formula-only input once; an input that a built-in reads shows only as that built-in. Saved choices use an exact revision. A heading names each group. Unavailable built-in sources stay visible, but you cannot choose them. Enter takes the best match. The arrow keys move through the list. Escape closes it. ＋ Create a new variable… opens the editor with an empty formula for that step. A new step joins the strategy only after you choose its source. A new filter goes before the last Rank. The list loads saved variables and financial inputs when opened. A failed load leaves the built-in choices visible.

How this works under the steps, the dates and the latest picks contains the longer explanations.

A Rank has Highest first or Lowest first and an inclusive rank range. A Filter has a comparison and a value. A variable Filter offers only the threshold units that fit its result. A built-in Filter keeps its own display unit. Sector and exchange Filters take one of the market's choices. A new Filter starts with an empty value, and submission asks for each value. A changed source keeps the typed value. The ↑, ↓ and ✕ buttons of a step have the names Move up, Move down and Remove. They change the order; focus stays on the moved step. A change made while a choice is loading makes that late choice stale; choose it again. Edit formula opens the formula of that step as text. A financial input becomes a one-name formula.

A strategy can have two or more sleeves. A sleeve is one chain of steps. The tab row above the steps shows one tab for each sleeve, and the steps below it belong to the selected tab. + Copy this sleeve adds a copy of the selected sleeve at the end and selects it, so a shared start, such as a market-cap Rank and a turnover Filter, is built one time. Sleeve name and Remove sleeve show when there are two or more sleeves. A sleeve has the value of its sector Is filter as its name, or Sleeve 1, Sleeve 2 and so on. A typed name replaces it. The 50-step limit counts the steps of all sleeves. A change of tab makes a late choice stale. One sleeve submits a chain (strategy-intent/2); two or more submit strategy-intent/3 and run on the local service. A copy or a held queue edit of a sleeve test opens its sleeves.

The default chain ranks the saved EBITDA/EV yield from highest to lowest after the size filters. Built-in sources work offline. The offline latest screen and auto-run cover filters the flat latest options express and one highest EBITDA/EV-yield Rank, first or last. Other chains run on the local service with Screen latest or Add to queue. A legacy pool shows a note: it first selects the 250 highest report EBITDA/EV yields. The cached-price pool avoids that pre-selection. Old results, queued settings and held drafts keep their recorded meaning.

In the editor, type the formula on one line, for example Total debt / Enterprise value. Suggestions below the line offer input names, My variables and function words for the partial name before the caret. Enter or Tab inserts one, and Escape closes the list. Enter never adds a line. All inputs lists the same names by category; a click inserts a name at the caret. The window has no built-ins. A name is optional; an empty name becomes the formula text. Close discards unsaved edits, and the browser's own undo replaces Undo and Redo. Annual statistics require consecutive fiscal years. A month lookback reconstructs an earlier observation date. It does not create quarterly or TTM accounts.

The editor checks the formula 400 ms after typing stops. The server reads the text and checks the language, units and required inputs. The line under the formula shows Checking…, Ready with the result unit and Show as, or the problem with suggested fixes. A fix replaces only the bad part. The check never moves the caret. A picture below shows how the server read the formula, with stacked fractions. Blank text sends no request. Use and Save check first when the text changed. Input support does not guarantee availability for every company.

The main button names its destination: Add as filter, Add as rank or Update step with the step number. Opening a formula and using it unchanged keeps its exact revision. Saving is optional. Save to My variables retains an immutable formula revision in the separate variable library. A saved variable shows Save changes, Save as new, Favourite and Delete. Names and favourites use an optimistic entry version. A concurrent change produces a conflict and keeps your local edit. A saved variable's name in a formula refers to its current revision. An exact old revision remains exact after a rename, edit or deletion. Saving a detached expression whose dependency is absent from the archive fails clearly; it does not silently import that dependency.

Use changes only the strategy draft. The selected source and highest or lowest direction stay visible. Filters keep their strict comparison, entered display threshold and canonical decimal threshold. Variable strategies require an explicit Screen latest or Add to queue. Variable strategies run with Original in all three scalar modes. A restored strategy that names the experimental engine shows the engine choice, so you can choose Original. The draft captures and restores that choice. Changing it does not relabel a displayed result or infer its producer. Every scalar result panel shows its recorded producer. Missing producer evidence stays explicitly unknown. Auto-run applies to the standalone built-in controls. Existing inclusive minimum-yield or maximum-multiple settings must be resolved explicitly before changing to an incompatible ranking. The draft is kept when that transition cannot preserve meaning.

The draft captures complete program content, ordered roots and presentation before a manual or queue submission receives its retry identity. The draft packs owner-produced editable definitions and names once per exact revision. Shared dependencies do not multiply the request size. Changed restored roots use the checked authoring projection. Unchanged captures for the same market retain their original complete content. An uncertain response retries the same payload. Later library changes cannot alter accepted work. A held queued edit protects its form until Save or Cancel ends that session. Ordinary result restoration uses that same protection.

Completed values, company explanations and downloads use the original immutable evidence. A selected-company trace follows its recorded scope, chunk, request and operation references. It shows captured arithmetic and financial input dates without calculating again. Complete original JSON is available under Advanced, and the complete evidence download keeps every original explanation. Reopening requires no current variable library or calculation.

variable_authoring.py owns financial-free authoring. The library owns exact raw snapshots and atomic saves. The definition owner converts checked detached programs into editable raw content with exact decimal compaction and revision checks. formula_text.py reads and prints the typed text, and vocabulary.py names each input once. variable-workspace.js owns the editor session and suggestions and turns a list choice into an exact checked source. filter-picker.js owns searching and choosing in a step's source list. range.js supplies the choices and renders the step rows. StrategyDraft owns the sleeves and their ordered steps, form sessions and submission capture. Whole-draft rules, such as captures and the step limit, read every sleeve. variable-evidence.js explains detached values; evidence-results.js presents bounded completed pages.

What does a submitted custom strategy retain?

Current source on main includes one variable workspace, complete strategy capture and Original scalar execution. Create and save variables, then choose exact revisions for ranking or filters. This source work does not change a running server. Original is the only engine the website runs. Native-cache coverage remains unknown.

Choose exact scalar sources→Capture program and labels→Normalize thresholds→Check complete request

Ranking and conditions can name an exact formula revision or a built-in scalar. Built-ins describe saved metric pairs or saved filter values. Yield and multiple remain independent saved values. No reciprocal is invented. Filters retain their original comparison scale. A custom condition also keeps its canonical decimal threshold and submitted display unit. For example, 8% is 0.08. A saved percent filter compares against 8 in its existing lane.

A custom ranking has an explicit highest or lowest direction. Capture/1 records inclusive ranks, selection order, pool and size or metadata bounds. Capture/2 records the pool and ordered steps. There is no hidden minimum-yield condition. See dated submissions for built-in bounds and conversion rules. Version-1 formula roots retain ranking-then-condition order. Version-2 roots follow step order. Both retain repeated exact references. The complete variable program and presentation come from their existing capture owner.

backtest/application/strategy_requests.py owns immutable strategy-capture/1, /2 and /3 values. This namespaced format allocates no application result integer. require_strategy() checks restored content without a current library or display catalog. It preserves original labels after library edits or deletion. Current capability admission is separate. Unsupported experimental custom intent fails explicitly before financial work.

The service accepts ordered strategies through strategy-intent/2 and strategy-capture/2. The website step builder submits them. Universe holds only pool; market stays in options.market. A chain has at least one Rank and at most 50 steps. Each Rank keeps an inclusive range from its incoming survivors. The last Rank sets final order, ranks and ranking value. Later Filters keep those ranks and add no replacements. Numeric Filters support strict and inclusive comparisons. Sector and exchange use field equality or inequality. Size floors are Filter steps.

The service also accepts sleeve strategies through strategy-intent/3 and strategy-capture/3. A sleeve is one named chain of Filter and Rank steps. A sleeve strategy has two or more sleeves, and the 50-step limit counts the steps of all sleeves. At each rebalance, each sleeve selects from the same stocks. The portfolio holds all selected stocks with equal weights. If two sleeves select the same stock, the portfolio holds it one time, at its first position. The holding rank is the position in this joined list: sleeve order, then the final order of each sleeve. The ranking value comes from the first sleeve that selected the stock. A period with fewer stocks than the sum of the last Rank sizes is a short period; the program adds no stocks. Sleeve names are labels and do not change calculation equality. The builder submits a sleeve strategy when its draft has two or more sleeves.

Capture/1 translates only in memory. Both capture versions use the ordered loop and read stored lanes through book_store.lanes. Metric sources keep its complete-pair admission. Filter lanes keep their existing independent values. Original bytes, defaults and stored comparison scales stay intact. Legacy flat requests keep the unchanged SQL selector for dated and latest runs, offline screens and parity checks. This work changes no prepared data identity.

Each selected stock's Details shows its step trail. Each step shows its source, recorded value and unit. A Rank shows its rank and kept range; a Filter shows passed. The Ranking value column and the formula or built-in step values of the trail show 2 decimals. Below 0.01, they show 2 significant digits. Below 0.000001, they show 0.00. Weights, returns and contributions show 2 decimals. Downloads and the calculation evidence keep the recorded precision. The trail reads the stored row and the captured strategy only. A traced formula reference of a chain records the value that the step used. Holdings and screen CSV files add step_<n>_value and step_<n>_outcome columns for a chain. For a sleeve strategy, they add one sleeves column, for example Financials #2; Technology #1. A sleeve stock shows one trail for each sleeve that selected it. Explore this result shows time windows only for a sleeve result. A capture/1 or older result says the trail is not recorded. It is never reconstructed.

Submission equality includes the complete payload and presentation. Calculation equality excludes names, descriptive provenance, submitted threshold spelling and lowerable content bounds. Definition and display revisions, exact sources, direction and canonical thresholds still change calculation meaning. A retry must retain its original payload. It must not capture newer labels after an uncertain response.

A caller can lower the capture limit. The library's separate 3 MiB capture capability does not enlarge the application request. See submission limits. Excess content fails without truncation.

The captured-intent owner creates no worker or financial ownership. Original consumes it through the existing jobs, queue and result-access owners. The editor uses StrategyDraft for patches, held restoration and capture before submission identity. Existing records are not rewritten. Stored version-1/2/3 results retain their existing readers.

What reusable measures can a formula use?

The formula language keeps 33 named measures. The editor lists each measure that combines several inputs as an input of its own. Each capture keeps exact definitions and its reachable dependencies. One program can contain at most 32 definitions. Positive division requires a positive denominator. Reported EBIT, free cash flow, debt and EPS retain their source fields. Report EBITDA uses accepted report history. Other legacy ratios retain the financial owners’ rules.

A latest root and every root of a fixed or random scope read the stored owner lanes of their book. A derived date uses dated ownership, even when its date equals the root date. A missing prepared company or lane does not fall back to a new calculation. Original is the only engine the website runs. Original execution can use captured measures. Private synthetic checks do not establish installed-data coverage.

What annual growth can a formula calculate?

A formula can calculate growth or compound annual growth from 2 to 10 consecutive annual observations. The number of annual intervals is one less than the observation count. Each result is a scalar fraction: 0.1 means 10%. Every observation must be available. Growth requires a positive first value. Compound annual growth also requires a positive last value. An unavailable input or invalid endpoint produces an unavailable result.

Original execution supports these statistics in version 2 and 3 definitions. Existing version 1 definitions and saved records keep their meaning.

How do custom variables run and retain their results?

Captured strategies use the local execution service in Latest, fixed dates and random dates. The shared editor supplies one captured strategy through the ordinary form. Built-in standalone screens keep their existing behavior. Original is the only engine the website runs. No running server or installed data changes from this source work.

Read complete prepared scope→Evaluate formula values→Apply ordered selection steps→Explain selected stocks→Close financial owners→Publish complete evidence

The SQLite observation view borrows Original's admitted connection. The column evaluator in backtest/variables/columns.py calculates formula values without step traces. It reads the typed facts of backtest/inputs/facts.py through the operation's daily connection. The owner lanes of a scope root are the stored lanes of its book, read once per book pool. A stored book row is its root's admission, with its stored candidate rank and entry valuation. A scope never screens its rows again. Values-only evaluation builds no evidence. It loads the needed annual fields once for each company in the view. Income fiscal dates still define the annual spine. It uses one set of rules for anchors, annual members, dated lookups and owner measures, and binary64 arithmetic. After each scope, the view checks the research-file status, the admitted daily binding and the research identity. The evaluator owns reports and annual alignment. The book admitted each stored row with the screen’s rules: an eligible report, the legacy buffer, cached prices and an eligible valuation. The row’s enterprise value is the book’s entry valuation. Uncached companies keep their place in the original 250-candidate buffer. No formula expands the prepared universe. Scope receipts distinguish all source companies from prepared rows with usable return evidence. Their admission count applies only to those prepared rows.

The ordered selector loads stored lanes once per scope. Consecutive Filters form one group. Stored checks run together first. Surviving rows then evaluate the needed formula roots together in one program, sharing dependencies. Each row’s value is cached for later uses. Cancellation checks run at step boundaries. Annual statistics are within one company. They do not depend on other survivors. Legacy filter-first captures still test stored conditions and bounds before formula conditions. A scope row is read with only the fields that selection and admission need. The full row of a stock, with its company name, is read only when the stock is selected. Captured execution permits at most 8,192 candidates in a scope. Missing values fail only the active step that needs them.

Built-in sources keep their actual saved values and comparison scale. Detached evidence records their declared canonical value too. In latest and fixed-date runs, the column evaluator also explains each selected stock. Its detail mode records the inputs, their fiscal, known and observation dates, reasons, source file digests and every operation, in the block shape that the evidence viewer reads. The same code computes the values that ranked the stock, so no second evaluator cross-checks them. A trace block larger than one evidence record is split in half. Older results keep their reference-evaluator explanations and open unchanged. Random-date runs keep each selected stock’s formula values and reasons without a formula operation trace. Nothing invents a reciprocal yield. Generic holdings show ranking value, unit and direction. Actual prices, returns, exits and portfolio arithmetic stay with their existing owners.

Capture/2 records step evidence for selected holdings only. It has one entry per step: the rank for a Rank and null for a Filter. A built-in or formula step's value, unit and source stay in its lane reference. A Universe field step has no lane reference. Its value is the holding's own field. Random-date holdings keep these values too. Old results without step evidence keep opening; their steps are never reconstructed. Both backtest.run paths log market, the last Rank’s built-in/formula kind and step count. Universe is not counted.

Application artifact 4, scalar selected-book contract 2 and evidence codec 2 are separate allocations. They are not derived from a formula namespace. Old artifacts 1, 2 and 3 and codec 1 retain their meanings. The existing durable version-3 container stores either supported application/codec pair through explicit dispatch. Existing records are not migrated or rewritten.

Latest evidence is screen-only. It has zero trials and zero periods. It contains no future return or contribution. Latest cannot be saved as a historical backtest. Fixed and random dates reuse existing calendars, missing-book workers, parent-only writes, per-trial transactions and financial reduction. Original is the only engine the website runs. Unsupported experimental formula intent fails before readiness or financial work.

Complete evidence uses at most 256 MiB of encoded content. A record uses at most 8 MiB and a piece at most 1 MiB. A whole run has no task, inspected-row or scope ceiling. You can stop a run. Before a random-date or month-interval run starts, a size check estimates the stored result. It refuses a run whose estimate exceeds the writer’s byte bound. The writer’s bound still applies during the run. These are content limits, not measured process-memory claims. Exceeding a limit fails the request. No evidence is truncated and no partial completion is published.

Scalar failures retain a safe message, a code, an expression path and ordered validation issues. Ordinary submission errors and failed job or queue status use the same fields. Queue failure details survive restart. Legacy errors keep their original text and response shape.

Editing, saving, favouriting and applying never launch a backtest.

Jobs automatically retain bounded evidence for a captured strategy. Queue receipts retain exact submitted programs, names and thresholds. Accepted retries keep the same payload. Later library edits and deletion cannot change it. A presentation-only waiting edit can retain its recorded random plan. A calculation change drops that plan. An explicit Stop stays cancelled. Shutdown interruption returns work to waiting.

Completed views acquire the same immutable result owner as older results. Its limits remain 16 display readers and 32 active request pins. Bounded pages expose scopes, rows and explanations. Scope/chunk-qualified references remain unambiguous. Reopening uses no current library, catalog, preparation or calculation. Each request has an independent stream position.

The scalar CSV keeps original values, units, direction and explanation references. Download complete evidence to retain the full captured strategy, input identity and every explanation offline. That companion file contains the original checksummed framed bytes. Counted attachment lengths detect interrupted transfers. Financial views, connections and workers close before completion becomes visible.

Where do website and tool sources live?

website/browser/ holds plain scripts, styles and HTML fragments. website/rendering/ owns detached data, static markup, ordered assets, exports and build freshness. website/server/ owns HTTP adapters and server lifetime. The source-owning entries remain at their documented paths. Latest output stays self-contained.

tools/ops/ owns maintained operations. tools/experiments/ holds only the retained FMP API acquisition experiments: the probes, download_one and fetch_bulk. Thin documented commands call their real owners. The deployment entry can verify and start its implementation from the selected archive. This keeps an older controller able to install the new source layout. Historical evidence keeps its original paths and hashes.

The custom-variable program is complete and integrated into main. The source provides trusted prepared inputs and point-in-time formula evaluation. It provides immutable validation, typed-facts scalar evaluation and a separate durable variable library. It provides captured strategy intent, one shared workspace and ordinary Original execution with immutable evidence. It provides the separate complete semantic catalog and endpoint-aware annual and dated preparation, with all 57 direct inputs and the two adapters for formula evaluation. It provides reusable measures over stored owner lanes and the dated owner policy, and shared authoring. Execution accepts the expanded captured vocabulary. The draft, editor, readable trace and bounded result presenter keep separate responsibilities. backtest/application/scalar_execution.py owns the complete-scope read for selection. backtest/variables/columns.py evaluates formula values for selection. Current built-in metric pairs keep their existing behavior. Read the current source map for the package owners.

What is the January record, and what checks the book code?

results/summary-exits.txt is the frozen record of the January study. It keeps a stock at its last price when trading stops. Nothing regenerates or changes it. results/baseline-history/, results/legacy/ and results/stops/ are frozen too. The legacy files use an older exit rule and are not the study result.

Preparation builds no January books and runs no second engine. After a change to book policy, run the development check, python3 scripts/check.py, on the real-data bench. It compares the 12-month January schedule with the independent reference engine on the same cached inputs. Only calculation differences fail the check. The frozen-report comparison is informational. The research workflow gives its settings.

Compatible preparation updates changed typed rows in one transaction. Cold, schema or fact-code builds use a temporary file and atomic replacement. Failure keeps the previous committed data.

How does the website adapt to a phone?

Desktop filters use four columns. Tablet filters use two columns. Phone filters use one column. Phone summary cards stack vertically. Buttons and form controls have a minimum height of 44 pixels.

Wide charts and tables scroll inside their panels. Scroll instructions remain visible. Stock symbols stay visible as stock tables scroll sideways. Tap a chart mark to read its detail below the chart. Mouse and keyboard interaction also work.

These layouts apply to latest picks, custom schedules and random trials. The built HTML includes the styles and interactions. Rebuild the website after a source change. A page already open in a browser needs a reload.

How do I inspect sector concentration?

Use Build strategy, Runs & saved and Result review to change tasks. Runs & saved shows the queue and the saved library as one table. Navigation keeps the strategy form mounted. Opening a result does not restore its settings into the draft. Tune this strategy is the explicit copy action. Desktop review keeps the original settings in a side column. Phones have a Settings section. The bottom status bar opens the existing queue panel and shows queue progress. It has no separate execution owner.

Selection starts with all original random trials. Each bar shows one trial's average sector allocation at entry. The combined mean averages rebalances within each complete trial, then weights complete trials equally. Cash-only books remain cash. Short books use their actual stock count. Unknown labels stay in the denominator. Incomplete trials remain listed and are excluded from the combined mean. These are entry allocations, not daily exposure or one combined portfolio.

Select a sector to compare it across trials. Inspect a trial, then a rebalance, to see its original stocks. Filtering keeps original ranks, returns and weights. Stock Details contains the remaining financial fields and original formula Explain action. Stock return contributions still use the whole original book.

backtest/application/result_sectors.py reads original acquired evidence in one traversal. All-trial replies contain compact statistics; one-trial replies also contain period counts. The browser never collects every holding page to draw sector charts. Inline saved results use the same aggregation. Existing request pins, freshness, cancellation and byte bounds apply. There is no new cache, durable format, financial calculation or readiness gate.

Can I inspect a shorter window or fewer stock ranks?

Open Explore this result in Result review under Overview or Returns. Choose saved entry and exit boundaries and original ranks. For a saved 24-trial, 2000–2025, top-50 random test, Explore all trials is available in Overview and Returns. Selecting 2010–2015 and ranks 20–30 updates every trial, combined statistics and the distribution chart without another backtest. A notice above the chart gives the window and ranks of an applied selection. The headline of the result always shows the original result.

Original saved returns→Choose periods and ranks→Shared Python return reduction→Temporary summary

Random selectors name saved rebalance blocks. Actual trade dates vary by trial. The summary shows one shared window from the earliest selected entry to the latest selected exit. A first-period selection keeps the original common start. Strategy and paired SPY hold cash before each first selected trade and after each last selected exit. Incomplete trials remain listed but are excluded from both distributions. Mean CAGR averages trial CAGRs; it is not one portfolio return.

Ranks retain their meaning at each rebalance. Surviving holdings have equal weight. Missing ranks receive no replacements. A complete empty selection holds cash at 0% until the next rebalance. SPY keeps its period return. CAGR includes the full elapsed window. The trial table shows empty-period counts. Missing evidence still fails. Older saved originals keep their recorded totals; Apply derives a temporary cash-based summary. Older January year labels allow total return but need exact boundary dates for CAGR. Reset restores recorded totals and rounding. Holding details, downloads and comparisons use the original result.

website/browser/result-explorer.js owns temporary controls and rejects obsolete replies. backtest/application/result_exploration.py checks selections and uses the mean, compounding and CAGR in backtest/portfolio_results.py. Browser-held results use a bounded request. Codec-backed batches take two sequential evidence scans with compact trial metadata. Existing reader pins, request ceilings and shutdown drain apply. No market inputs, saved records or formats change.

What do the charts and downloads show?

Result review shows the answer first. A headline below the title gives strategy CAGR, SPY CAGR, their difference and the growth of $1. For random dates, it gives the trial statistics. The headline uses stored summary values of the original result. Overview then shows the main chart and its table. Explore and Recorded coverage and notes follow them.

Value of $1 day by day starts Overview. It shows the strategy and SPY on every market day, so a rally or a fall inside a holding period shows. For random dates, it shows the median trial and a band from the lowest to the highest trial on each day. Returns shows the curve of the selected trial. Point at the chart to read one day. The vertical scale is logarithmic: equal heights are equal percentage moves. A result saved before the curve existed shows no chart. website/browser/asset-curve.js draws the chart from the curve reader route.

For random dates, Returns shows one trial below the title Trial N of M. Show stocks and period returns below the trial table opens the selected trial there.

Browser downloads use the original result. Exploration selections and pending strategy settings do not change a download. Historical views show period returns and the growth of an equal-weight portfolio.

A stock’s contribution is its holding return divided by the actual stock count. Gain and loss pies are scaled separately. Their slices are not shares of net return.

The return distribution chart shows trial counts for the current seed. CAGR and total return show strategy and paired SPY on the same bins and axes. You can also select the CAGR difference from SPY. Each series has its own mean marker. A dashed bell curve fits each series with nonzero standard deviation. This fit does not show that returns follow a normal distribution. Incomplete trials are excluded. Identical returns show one bar without a fitted curve.

The average random-trial CAGR is an average of trial results. It is not one portfolio return. Trial percentiles are not confidence intervals.

Which limits should I keep in mind?
  • The strategy uses equal starting weights and no commissions.
  • The saved-price group does not cover the full market.
  • Sector, exchange and listing status come from saved company metadata.
  • Fallback report delays are assumptions, not verified filing dates.
  • Some supplier figures can include later revisions.
  • New early stops outside the original review can need further checks.

08 / Words used in this guide

The terms, without the code.

Cache
Saved data that the program can use again.
Book
The stock records for one buy date and one sell or mark date.
Pool / Stock group
The set of candidate stocks used for selection. It is separate from the final stock count.
Snapshot
A saved stock record for a particular date or holding period.
Filter
A condition that a stock must meet before ranking.
Rank
A stock’s position after filtering and sorting by the selected metric.
Rebalance
Select stocks again and give each selected stock the same starting weight.
Trial
One complete backtest with one set of sampled trade dates.
Seed / Date-set number
A number used to repeat random date choices with the same saved data and settings.
SQLite
A database engine that reads and writes local files. It does not need a separate database server.
Market cap
The estimated market value of the company’s equity.
EV / Enterprise value
In this model, estimated market cap plus report net debt.
EBITDA
Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization. The model derives it from saved annual metrics.
EBITDA/EV and EV/EBITDA
Reciprocal ratios. A higher positive EBITDA/EV means a lower positive EV/EBITDA.
P/B
Price divided by book value. This filter needs saved annual equity and a rebuild.
P/S
Price divided by annual revenue (sales).
CAGR
The constant annual growth rate that would produce the same total growth over the test window.
SPY
The S&P 500 ETF used for comparison. Its saved return series includes dividends.
API / Local service
The browser’s way to ask Python for a dated calculation. These requests use saved data on your computer.
